answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-weighted attestation graph. Each identity is a vertex that locks a small refundable deposit and earns attestations from established peers before trading at full limits. Trust thaws like a glacier: reputation accrues slowly over weeks of honest work, so a fresh swarm of fakes stays near zero weight. Before large payments, counterparties run a sparrow probe — a tiny test task worth pennies — cheap for honest agents, but forces an attacker to fund and age each fake identity separately. One fake costs little; ten thousand cost a fortune.
